project_title: Logo needed for UK start up catering company

project_metadata.job_title: Logo needed for UK start up catering company
project_metadata.job_description:
** Thank you for sending your proposals. We look forward to reviewing them all soon. Please bear with us though as we are a bit busy but we will get back to you as soon as possible!**

We are looking for an experienced logo designer to create an original logo for our UK-based street food business, Global Dough.

Global Dough serves globally inspired street food built around dough and flatbreads, including pizzas, naan breads, wraps and other freshly prepared street food cooked in wood-fired and tandoor ovens.

What we need:
A clean, unique and professional logo
Minimalist
Modern-retro styling (not cartoonish)
Strong enough to work on the side of a food truck (see attached pic)
Simple, bold and highly legible from a distance
Suitable for social media, our website (not produced yet), menus, signage, clothing and packaging
Typography-led design preferred
We are open to subtle graphic elements, but do not want obvious globes, chef hats, food clipart or generic AI-style icons
We only want one example of a logo with subtle graphic elements. The other concepts need to be just typography as that's our preference.

Colours:
Burnt orange
Black
White

Logo should have the name of the company and our strapline:
Global Dough
Seriously Tasty Street Food

Deliverables:
3–5 initial concepts
Up to 3 revision rounds
Full colour version
Black version
White version
Vector files (AI, EPS, SVG)
PNG files with transparent background
JPGS
Font details supplied

Copyright & Ownership:
The final logo must be completely original.

No stock logos, copyrighted elements, template-based logos, or AI-generated logo artwork.

When applying please provide:

Examples of food hospitality logos you have designed.
Confirmation that your work is original and suitable for trademark use.
Your estimated turnaround time.
Your fixed-price quote.
Upon final payment, all intellectual property rights must transfer exclusively to us. The logo should be suitable for future trademark registration.

Budget: £150–£200

messages.text:
Hi [CLIENT_NAME_001], apologies for that. Please allow me a moment to check the files, and I’ll send them again shortly.

Thank you for being patient, and I appreciate you alerting me to the issue.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Thank you for sending these. Does the fixed cost also cover establishing our brand colours and fonts? We hope to hire you, but wanted to double-check that colour and font guidelines could also be produced.

I’m looking forward to receiving the contract.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Hi, [FREELANCER_NAME_001] attached a draft logo made using AI—we were obviously only tinkering around with chat gpt. That said, we want fresh, original ideas, which is why we posted our proposal, although we do like those colours because they fit the look and feel of the Global Dough truck. The company is called 'Global Dough', so the logo should not contain the word 'truck'. The 'truck' component is only one area of the business. Put another way, 'Global Dough', the business needing the logo, will run a mobile catering truck, sell food online, and may also sell to other caterers/kitchens. This is why the business name is simply 'Global Dough', while the strapline stays the same. Are you happy to discuss anything before accepting the offer?

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: This is the truck, although, as noted above, the business encompasses more than only this.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Understood. I’ll develop a few concepts that closely reflect your vision, while introducing a creative element so the designs remain unique and visually appealing.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: My usual preference is to accept the offer once [FREELANCER_NAME_001] shared the initial drafts, because that allows clients to assess the direction first and be fully comfortable before proceeding.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: However, I’m flexible and glad to follow whichever arrangement makes you most comfortable. I can accept the offer after I present the initial concepts if that is your preference, or I can accept it right away if you would rather—I’m fine with either option.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Yes, let’s follow your approach and review the intial drafts first. Thank you

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Thank you.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
Hi [CLIENT_NAME_001], please review the initial drafts and share your thoughts with me. I’d be very interested to receive your feedback.

If you want any revisions, refinements, iterations, or changes, please feel free to say so. I’m happy to continue working with you until the result aligns perfectly with your vision.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Hi, many thanks for these. Matt (my partner - who is the chef and the creator of the business!!) and I have reviewed them. [FREELANCER_NAME_001] attached our feedback in a powerpoint, and hopefully everything is clear. If you’re uncertain about anything we mean, please let me know. All best, [CLIENT_NAME_001]

messages.speaker: freelancer

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Hi [CLIENT_NAME_001], could you please take a look and share your feedback with me?

messages.speaker: client
messages.text:
Thank you for these. We like the graduated orange colour and the lines beside the strapline.

Our preferences are the 1st and 3rd one, since the font used in the 2nd one feels too plain. However, someone unfamiliar with our name might not understand that the flame in the 3rd one represents an ‘O’, even though we like it.

Perhaps the flame could sit inside an ‘O’, be reshaped to look more like an ‘O’, or be superimposed over an ‘O’. Could you test all of those suggestions?

For logo 3, could we also see how it looks with ‘dough’ made slightly larger? To make the strapline more prominent, could you either outline every letter with a thin black pencil line or slightly brighten the orange tones used in the strapline lettering? We like the global dough font because it has character, particularly the G. We wondered whether a little ‘character’ could be added to a couple of the other letters, but thought it would be better to handle the revisions one stage at a time, as the existing font may be okay. Thank you—we’re moving in the right direction.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Thanks for the feedback. I’ll examine it and contact you if any questions come up.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Hi [CLIENT_NAME_001], [FREELANCER_NAME_001] applied the feedback. Please look through the revised designs and tell me what you think.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Thanks for sending these. We’ve simply been swamped with work, so we’ll respond over the weekend.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Sure, take your time.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text:
Hi, apologies for taking so long to respond.

Matt prefers number 4, where the strapline matches the colour of ‘global’ and both use graduated colours.

I was wondering, though, whether you could add a little more character to the ‘global dough’ font. The food will be genuinely authentic and freshly cooked, featuring flavours from around the world. I like the unusual shape of the ‘G’ in both words; could a similar treatment be applied to more letters without taking it too far? thanks, [CLIENT_NAME_001]

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
Hi [CLIENT_NAME_001], certainly! I’ll review it, explore what’s possible, and come back to you with a revised draft.
Thank you.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
I think these two options represent roughly the greatest amount of character that can be introduced without harming the logo’s overall readability and quality. Adding more than this would begin to undermine the clean, refined appearance and reduce its versatility across different uses.

My focus has been on bringing subtle personality into the letterforms while retaining the brand’s premium and authentic feel. In my view, this adds a distinctive quality without sacrificing the logo’s professionalism or overall balance.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Please take a look and share your thoughts with me.

messages.speaker: client

Hi, thanks for these. We’re nearly there!

2\. Could you flip the top on the right hand side of the H in DOUGH, making it mirror the top of the U in DOUGH?
3\. Lastly, could you apply the same feature to the top of the D in DOUGH, similar to the top of the B in GLOBAL?
Please refer to the attached annotated screenshot.
After that, we’ll review it again and hopefully it will retain the ‘clean’ appearance while also having the character.
Many thanks, [CLIENT_NAME_001]

That said, I believe the primary logo should be the version in the top row of the final design: graduated orange ‘global’, black ‘dough’, and the strapline in graduated orange.

Given that the files will have large file sizes, how will you share them? Wetransfer?

Thank you, [CLIENT_NAME_001]

Hi [CLIENT_NAME_001], excellent! When convenient, could you approve the first milestone and activate the second, allowing me to proceed with the outstanding work?

Yes, the logo will be supplied with the black box and without it.

For the color variants, are you requesting every color version considered during the design process, or only the standard full-color, black, and white versions?

I’ll provide all required file formats as well, including fully editable source files, enabling you to use the logo for print, web, social media, signage, merchandise, and any other purpose. The final delivery will also contain the font information and color codes used in the chosen design.

I did want to clarify that logo guidelines were not part of the original project scope, as they are generally supplied through a separate project.

There are two options:

Basic Logo Usage Guidelines – $100
Covers logo variations, clear space, minimum size, color palette, typography, and basic do's and don'ts.

Complete Brand Guidelines – $150
Contains everything offered in the basic guide, along with a broader brand system addressing typography hierarchy, imagery style, iconography, layout principles, brand applications, stationery and t-shirt mockups, and detailed usage rules.

I’d be happy to produce either option if you wish, helping ensure the logo is applied consistently and professionally to all future branding materials.
